chunks: Muhammad ibn Abi Abdullah from Muawiya ibn Hukaym from Safwan and Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ribat from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the choice (al-khiyar), so he (peace be upon him) said: 'And what is it, and what is that? That is something which was for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).'

key_terms.أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ: Abu Ja'far (Imam al-Baqir), a key narrator of hadith
key_terms.الْخِيَار: The right of choice or option in a transaction or contract

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'al-khiyar' and was it exclusive to the Prophet?
ai.summary: In this concise narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the specific legal concept of *al-khiyar* (the right of option/choice) was originally a unique privilege granted exclusively to the Messenger of Allah (PBUH). This highlights the distinct legislative authority of the Prophet, distinguishing his immediate legal status from that of the general community before such rulings were extended to the Ummah.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Muawiya Bin Hukeym, from Safwan, and Ali Bin Al Hassan Bin Rabat, from Abu Ayoub Al Khazzaz, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said,
‘I asked Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> about the choice, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And what is it, and what is that? But rather, that is something which was for Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah has narrated from Mu‘awiyah ibn Hakam from Safwan and Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Ribat from abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “I once asked abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about choices. He (the Imam) said, ‘Who is he and what is that; it was something only for the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause.’”
